Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned
Aga for the State.

2.  This application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred for quashing of the entire proceedings,
including charge-sheet dated 21.04.2018 and cognizance order dated 19.07.2019, of Criminal Case No. 8762 of 2019, arising out of Case Crime No.114 of 2017, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506,
406, 342 IPC, P.S. Mahila Thana, District Gorakhpur, pending in the court of ACJM-IInd,
Gorakhpur, on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.
3.

It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that applicant nos. 1 & 2 are sister-in-law (nanad) of opposite party no. 2/informant and the matter relates to matrimonial Nisha Pandey And Anr. vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98682335/
1 dispute.

entities.text: matrimonial Nisha Pandey And Anr. vs State Of U.P. And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now both the parties have amicably settled the dispute and compromised the matter and the informant of the case does not want to pursue the impugned proceedings.

It was submitted that the counter affidavit of opposite party no.2 is on record, wherein she has stated that she does not want to pursue the impugned proceedings and the impugned proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties before the Hon'ble Apex Court vide order dated 01.08.2024.

It was stated that in view of these facts and circumstances no useful purpose would be served by keeping the impugned proceedings pending and thus, the impugned proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.
4. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 /informant has concurred with the arguments of learned counsel for the applicants and submitted that both the parties have amicably settled the dispute and compromised the matter and the informant does not want to proceed with the case pending before the trial court and the impugned proceedings may be quashed.
5.
Learned A.G.A. has no objection if parties compromise the matter.
6. I have considered the submissions and perused the record.
7. It is well settled that in appropriate cases criminal proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise.
In the instant case, matter relates to matrimonial dispute, which is private in nature.
If parties compromise the matter, it would not have adverse impact on society.
There is nothing to indicate that parties have any criminal antecedents.
The informant of the case does not want to pursue the impugned proceedings.

The counter affidavit of the opposite party no.2 is on record,
wherein she has stated that she has compromised the matter before the Hon'ble Apex Court and the impugned proceedings may be quashed.

It also appears from record that on the basis of compromise between the parties, the proceedings of aforesaid case against Abhimanyu Pandey, who is husband of opposite party no.2, have already been quashed by this Court vide order dated 24.02.2025 on the basis of compromise between the parties.

Considering the law laid down in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, AIR 2019 SC 1296 and the facts of the matter, it would be in the interest of justice that the impugned proceedings be quashed.

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, AIR 2019 SC 1296
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In view of the aforesaid, entire impugned proceedings, including charge-sheet and cognizance order of the aforesaid case, against applicants, namely, Nisha Pandey & Smt. Sunita Pandey are hereby quashed.
9. The application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed.
